channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Jul 24–30
item.description: The most consequential thing on this week's government calendar is the Gondola Leadership Committee meeting on July 28, where the agenda includes an action item on background and history, a walkthrough of the Capital Investment Grant program and its funding commitments, and a project update — the kind of session where real money and long-term decisions start taking shape. Town Council also convenes July 27 as the Liquor Licensing Authority for a public hearing on KOTO Radio's special event permit for its Live at the Drive show at 207 N Pine Street on July 30. On the community side, the week has plenty going on, from The Music Man at the Sheridan to Shakespeare in the Park and the Farmers Market.

item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Town Park Join us ON the Town Park Stage for one of our town’s most beloved traditions: Telluride Theatre's 36th Annual SHAKESPEARE IN THE PARK! item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Gondola Leadership Committee - Jul 28 2026 — 2026-07-28
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-07-28
The Gondola Leadership Committee meets July 28 for what looks like a substantive session. Miles Graham opens with background and history — marked as an action item, which suggests something more than a recap. Ed Parks and Amber Blake then walk through the CIG (Capital Investment Grant) program and its funding commitments, followed by a project update. The heaviest time slot goes to a fiscal and economic impact analysis presented by Parks and Chris Brewer. Miles Graham rounds out the agenda with local jurisdiction updates before public comment. The gondola project — and the $5.2 million annual tax behind it — has been one of the most contested questions in the valley in recent years, so the funding and economic impact presentations will draw scrutiny.
⚡ Why it matters: Action items on gondola history and CIG funding commitments could shape capital decisions.
